falsifier: A graph partition violating the lifted quotient plus internal cover bound.
proof:
Cover the quotient edges by \(bc(Q_{\mathcal P})\) bipartite layers.
Lift each quotient layer by taking every cross-part edge of \(G\) whose
pair of parts lies in that layer. The lifted graph is bipartite using the
unions of the quotient layer's two sides. These layers cover every
cross-part edge. The internal edges form the disjoint union of the
\(G[P]\)'s and therefore require the displayed supremum. Combine the covers.
statement:
Let \(\mathcal P\) be a partition of \(V(G)\), and let \(Q_{\mathcal P}\)
be the quotient graph whose vertices are the parts and whose edges are the
pairs of parts joined by at least one edge of \(G\). Let \(bc(Q_{\mathcal P})\)
be the least cardinality of a cover of \(E(Q_{\mathcal P})\) by bipartite
subgraphs. Then
\[
tc(G)\le bc(Q_{\mathcal P})+\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}tc(G[P]).
\]
title: Quotient-Lift Compression Theorem

falsifier: A graph whose incidence-matching realization has a different quotient.
novelty: "every graph" quotient of matching stable partition
proof:
For every incidence of a vertex \(i\in V(Q)\) with an edge \(e\in E(Q)\),
create a distinct vertex \(x_{i,e}\). For each \(e=ij\), add only the edge
\(x_{i,e}x_{j,e}\). Add one isolated vertex to the part for every isolated
vertex of \(Q\). Put all \(x_{i,e}\)'s belonging to \(i\) in one part.
Different graph edges use disjoint endpoints, so the constructed graph is
a matching. Two parts are adjacent in the quotient exactly when their
indices are adjacent in \(Q\).
statement:
Every simple graph \(Q\) is the quotient graph of a matching under a
partition into stable sets.
title: Universal Quotient Realization by a Matching

falsifier: A positive induced vertex set homogeneous for adjacency or nonadjacency.
proof:
If the constant is zero, \(G[U]\) is stable and has triangle-cover number
at most one. If the constant is one, \(G[U]\) is complete. \(K_4\)-freeness
gives \(|U|\le3\), and hence \(tc(G[U])\le2\le\kappa\).
statement:
Let \(\kappa\) be infinite and let \(G\) be \(K_4\)-free with
\(tc(G)>\kappa\). For the binary pair map
\[
a(\{x,y\})=\mathbf 1_{xy\in E(G)},
\]
there is no \(U\subseteq V(G)\) such that \(tc(G[U])>\kappa\) and \(a\)
is constant on \([U]^2\).
title: Adjacency Pair-Homogeneity Impossibility

falsifier: A dominating set of cardinality at most \(2^\kappa\).
proof:
If \(S\) were a dominating set with \(|S|\le2^\kappa\), then
\(N[S]=V(G)\). This contradicts HG14, which says that
\(tc(G-N[S])>\kappa\).
statement:
Let \(\kappa\) be infinite. If \(G\) is \(K_4\)-free and
\(tc(G)>\kappa\), then
\[
\gamma(G)>2^\kappa,
\]
where \(\gamma(G)\) is the domination number.
title: Large Domination Obstruction

falsifier: A small closed-neighborhood deletion whose every residual component is κ-coverable.
proof: HG14 gives \(tc(G-N[S])>\kappa\). Apply the component supremum formula T4.
statement:
Let \(\kappa\) be infinite, let \(G\) be \(K_4\)-free with
\(tc(G)>\kappa\), and let \(|S|\le2^\kappa\). Then some connected
component \(C\) of \(G-N[S]\) satisfies
\[
tc(C)>\kappa.
\]
title: Closed-Neighborhood Escape Component

falsifier: A family or set witnessing one of the three invariants below \((2^\kappa)^+\).
novelty: "triangle-cover ideal" add cov non cardinal invariants
proof:
HG04 says that the union of at most \(2^\kappa\) ideal members remains in
the ideal, giving the additivity bound. A cover of \(V(G)\) by at most
\(2^\kappa\) ideal members would put \(V(G)\) in the ideal, giving the
covering bound. Every set of size at most \(2^\kappa\) is a union of at
most \(2^\kappa\) singletons, and singletons are ideal members, giving the
uniformity bound.
statement:
Let \(\kappa\) be infinite, \(tc(G)>\kappa\), and
\(\mathcal J_\kappa(G)=\{A\subseteq V(G):tc(G[A])\le\kappa\}\).
Then
\[
\operatorname{add}(\mathcal J_\kappa),
\operatorname{cov}(\mathcal J_\kappa),
\operatorname{non}(\mathcal J_\kappa)
\ge (2^\kappa)^+.
\]
title: Cardinal Invariants of the Induced-Null Ideal

falsifier: An inclusion-maximal induced-null set or an inclusion-minimal positive set.
proof:
If \(A\in\mathcal J_\kappa(G)\), choose \(v\notin A\); the set
\(A\cup\{v\}\) is still in the ideal by HG04. If \(U\notin\mathcal J_\kappa(G)\)
and \(v\in U\), apply HG05 inside \(G[U]\) to the singleton \(\{v\}\);
then \(U\setminus\{v\}\) remains positive.
statement:
If \(tc(G)>\kappa\), then \(\mathcal J_\kappa(G)\) has no
inclusion-maximal member, and the family
\(\mathcal J_\kappa(G)^+\) has no inclusion-minimal member.
title: No Maximal Null Set and No Minimal Positive Set

falsifier: A permitted profile system for which no such subgraph and link exist.
proof:
Apply HG08 to obtain an induced positive unary-profile fiber \(G[U]\).
Apply HG07 to the restricted edge maps to obtain a positive common
edge-profile subgraph \(F\). Since \(F\) is \(K_4\)-free and positive,
apply T7.
statement:
Let \(G\) be \(K_4\)-free with \(tc(G)>\kappa\). Fix at most \(\kappa\)
unary vertex maps with ranges of size at most \(\kappa\), and edge maps
whose combined profile space on \(E(G)\) has cardinality at most \(\kappa\).
Then there is a spanning subgraph \(F\) on a vertex set \(U\) such that
\(tc(F)>\kappa\); all vertices of \(U\) have one common unary profile;
all edges of \(F\) have one common edge profile; and \(F\) contains a
triangle-free forward link of chromatic number greater than \(\kappa\).
title: Mixed Unary–Edge Profile Canonization

falsifier: A page-free unary-homogeneous subwitness in which every edge-profile cell is κ-null.
proof: Apply HG07 and T7 inside the page-free induced subwitness from HG21.
statement:
Under the hypotheses of HG21, additionally fix edge maps whose combined
edge-profile space has size at most \(\kappa\). Then the page-free,
unary-homogeneous induced witness supplied by HG21 contains a positive
common edge-profile subgraph and hence a high-chromatic triangle-free
forward link, all avoiding the original stable certificate pages.
title: Page-Free Mixed Profile Canonization

falsifier: A stable partition quotient colorable with fewer colors than \(G\).
proof:
Every proper coloring of the quotient lifts to a proper coloring of \(G\)
by assigning every vertex the color of its part. Thus
\(\chi(G)\le\chi(Q_{\mathcal P})\). If \(|\mathcal P|=\chi(G)\), then the
quotient has only \(\chi(G)\) vertices and hence chromatic number at most
\(\chi(G)\).
statement:
Let \(\mathcal P\) be the stable color classes of a proper coloring of
\(G\). Then
\[
\chi(G)\le\chi(Q_{\mathcal P}).
\]
If the coloring uses exactly \(\chi(G)\) colors, then
\[
\chi(Q_{\mathcal P})=\chi(G).
\]
title: Optimal Stable-Partition Quotient Exactness

falsifier: A positive graph partitioned into κ-null cells with a κ-bipartite-coverable quotient.
proof:
If \(bc(Q_{\mathcal P})\le\kappa\), RG01 gives \(tc(G)\le\kappa\).
If \(\chi(Q_{\mathcal P})\le2^\kappa\), binary-code a proper quotient
coloring to cover the quotient edges by \(\kappa\) bipartite layers,
again contradicting the first conclusion.
statement:
Let \(\kappa\) be infinite and \(tc(G)>\kappa\). If every part
\(P\in\mathcal P\) satisfies \(tc(G[P])\le\kappa\), then
\[
bc(Q_{\mathcal P})>\kappa
\quad\text{and}\quad
\chi(Q_{\mathcal P})>2^\kappa.
\]
title: Null-Cell Quotient Obstruction

falsifier: A quotient graph that cannot be realized by a triangle-free matching.
proof: Apply the matching realization RG02. A matching is triangle-free.
statement:
Quotient isomorphism type alone cannot give any nontrivial universal lower
bound on the triangle-cover number of a partitioned graph: every quotient
graph \(Q\), including graphs of arbitrarily large chromatic number, has a
realization whose ambient graph has triangle-cover number at most one.
title: Quotient-Only Sterility Theorem

falsifier: Failure of unary canonization or a positive adjacency-homogeneous induced set.
novelty: "unary versus pair canonization" graph adjacency triangle-cover
proof: The unary assertion is HG08. The binary failure is RG03.
statement:
In a \(K_4\)-free graph with \(tc(G)>\kappa\), every family of at most
\(\kappa\) unary \(\kappa\)-valued vertex maps is simultaneously constant
on an induced positive subgraph, but complete homogeneity already fails
for the single binary adjacency relation.
title: Exact Unary–Pair Arity Boundary

falsifier: A first stage below \(\theta\) with no available vertex.
proof:
Recursively choose \(v_\alpha\) for \(\alpha<\theta\). At stage \(\alpha\),
the prior set has size at most \(2^\kappa\). HG14 leaves a nonempty
positive graph outside its closed neighborhood; choose \(v_\alpha\) there.
It is nonadjacent to every earlier vertex.
statement:
Let \(\theta=(2^\kappa)^+\). Every \(K_4\)-free graph \(G\) with
\(tc(G)>\kappa\) contains a stable set of cardinality \(\theta\).
title: Huge Stable Set Theorem

falsifier: A maximal stable set of cardinality at most \(2^\kappa\).
proof: A maximal stable set is dominating. Apply RG04.
statement:
Every maximal stable set in a \(K_4\)-free graph with \(tc(G)>\kappa\)
has cardinality at least \((2^\kappa)^+\).
title: Large Maximal Stable Sets

falsifier: A null deletion after which every stable set is too small.
proof: HG05 leaves a \(K_4\)-free positive induced residual. Apply RG14 there.
statement:
If \(A\in\mathcal J_\kappa(G)\) and \(G\) is \(K_4\)-free with
\(tc(G)>\kappa\), then \(G-A\) contains a stable set of cardinality
\((2^\kappa)^+\).
title: Stable Reserve after Every Null Deletion

falsifier: A smaller ideal cover or a smaller positive set.
proof: This is the \(\operatorname{cov}\) and \(\operatorname{non}\) portion of RG06.
statement:
At least \((2^\kappa)^+\) induced \(\kappa\)-null sets are required to
cover \(V(G)\), and every induced positive vertex set has cardinality at
least \((2^\kappa)^+\).
title: No Small Null Cover and No Small Positive Set

falsifier: A null deletion followed by a null-cell partition with low quotient.
proof: HG05 makes \(G-A\) positive. Apply RG11 to the residual.
statement:
Let \(A\in\mathcal J_\kappa(G)\), where \(tc(G)>\kappa\). Every partition
of \(V(G)\setminus A\) into induced \(\kappa\)-null cells has quotient
chromatic number greater than \(2^\kappa\).
title: Null-Deletion Hereditary Quotient Obstruction

falsifier: A high quotient with no finite high-chromatic subquotient, or a finite union of null cells that is positive.
novelty: "finite high chromatic quotient" null induced union
proof:
RG11 gives \(\chi(Q_{\mathcal P})>2^\kappa\), hence it is greater than
\(n\). By de Bruijn–Erdős finite-coloring compactness, a finite subgraph
has chromatic number greater than \(n\). Its finitely many cells have an
induced-null union by HG04.
statement:
Under the hypotheses of RG11, for every finite \(n\) there is a finite
subfamily \(\mathcal F_n\subseteq\mathcal P\) such that
\[
\chi(Q_{\mathcal P}[\mathcal F_n])>n,
\]
while
\[
\bigcup\mathcal F_n\in\mathcal J_\kappa(G).
\]
title: Finite High-Chromatic Quotient Skeletons Are Null

falsifier: A quotient-only or finite-skeleton invariant that universally forces positivity.
proof:
The first assertion is RG19. The second is reinforced by RG12, which
realizes every quotient graph over a matching.
statement:
In every null-cell partition of a positive graph, arbitrarily
high-chromatic finite quotient patterns may be supported on induced-null
vertex unions. Consequently neither quotient chromatic number nor any
finite quotient subgraph, considered without its edge-fiber realization,
can carry the triangle-cover obstruction.
title: Relational Migration Theorem

falsifier: A first stage below \(\theta\) at which the next stable row cannot be extracted.
proof:
At stage \(\alpha<\theta\), the union of the previously selected stable
sets is the union of at most \(2^\kappa\) members of
\(\mathcal J_\kappa(G)\), so HG04 makes it null. HG05 leaves a positive
induced residual, and RG14 supplies the next stable set.
statement:
Let \(\theta=(2^\kappa)^+\). Every \(K_4\)-free graph \(G\) with
\(tc(G)>\kappa\) contains a family
\(\langle S_\alpha:\alpha<\theta\rangle\) of pairwise disjoint stable
sets, each of cardinality \(\theta\).
title: Disjoint Huge-Stable-Grid Extraction

falsifier: A unary label system whose positive profile fibers lack the stable grid.
proof: HG08 gives an induced positive common-profile fiber. Apply RG21 inside it.
statement:
Under the unary-label hypotheses of HG08, one common unary profile contains
\((2^\kappa)^+\) pairwise disjoint stable sets, each of cardinality
\((2^\kappa)^+\).
title: Unary-Homogeneous Stable Grid

falsifier: Either a positive adjacency-homogeneous induced set or failure of mixed profile canonization.
proof: The impossibility is RG13 and the replacement is RG08.
statement:
Complete pair homogenization is impossible by RG13, but the following
replacement is always available: simultaneous unary homogeneity on an
induced positive vertex set, followed by edge-profile homogeneity on a
positive spanning subgraph and high-chromatic link extraction.
title: Exact Replacement for Failed Pair Homogenization

falsifier: A page-free positive set with a low quotient, or a quotient type alone forcing positivity.
proof: Apply RG11 inside \(G[U]\) for the first assertion and RG12 for the second.
statement:
Under the hypotheses of HG21, let \(U\) be its page-free,
unary-homogeneous induced positive set. Every partition of \(U\) into
induced \(\kappa\)-null cells has quotient chromatic number greater than
\(2^\kappa\), yet the quotient graph alone cannot certify positivity.
title: Page-Free Relational Residual

falsifier: A page-free unary-homogeneous subwitness lacking the huge stable grid.
novelty: "page-free stable grid" maximal layers unary canonization
proof: Apply RG21 inside the induced subwitness supplied by HG21.
statement:
Under the hypotheses of HG21, its page-free unary-homogeneous induced
subwitness contains \((2^\kappa)^+\) pairwise disjoint stable sets, each
of cardinality \((2^\kappa)^+\), all avoiding the original certificate
pages and sharing the same unary profile.
title: Page-Free Homogeneous Stable Grid

falsifier: A graph whose triangle structure is not captured by the fiber/endpoint incidence schema, or a smaller exact schema.
proof:
RG20 proves that quotient type and finite quotient skeletons are sterile.
RG24 shows that the live page-free residual still has a high-chromatic
quotient. The missing information is therefore the endpoint-sharing
coherence among quotient edge fibers. This is an executable SAT/ILP target.
statement:
For a null-cell partition \(\mathcal P\), retain the quotient graph together
with every bipartite edge fiber \(G[P,Q]\) and the ternary incidence rule
specifying which triples of fiber edges share endpoints to form graph
triangles. Classify the finite \(K_4\)-free fibered quotients that are
realizable, determine which have triangle-cover number above a prescribed
bound, and identify the minimal coherence patterns not reproducible by the
matching construction of RG02.
title: Fiber-Coherence Classification Target
